title: USA Stocks are DUMPING, Losing $1T as Second Inflation Wave Strikes
speaker: Sean Foo

macro_themes.view: Energy-driven inflation (CPI 3.7%, core rebounding) is squeezing US consumers and forcing the Fed to keep hiking, which will crush the hyper-financialized economy.
Escalation with Iran keeps pushing oil higher and is why Trump wants a Russia energy deal before the midterms.
Rising rates break the debt-funded data-center model (CoreWeave bonds at 15% yields are the canary), so AI stocks fall like a house of cards.
Treasury buying back long bonds shows weak global demand for US debt.
Inflation makes China's cheap exports more competitive, pushing its trade surplus toward $1.2T in 2026 and funding its AI push.

calls.reason: Hot inflation forces higher rates that hit consumers, mortgages and the AI capex engine; S&P already erased $1T in a session.
calls.quote: it's no surprise that stocks are starting to fall, and this could be the start of a major correction.

calls.reason: AI build-out relies on cheap money; higher rates and rising yields make data centers harder to finance, and Chinese AI competition adds pressure.
calls.quote: that is why AI stocks are falling like a house of cards. The whole model relies on cheap money, and cheap money, well, it's gone.

calls.reason: Debt-funded Nvidia chip purchases with bond yields jumping from 9.6% to 15%; chips need replacing in 3-5 years, requiring more expensive borrowing.
calls.quote: Coreweave is the canary in a coal mine.

calls.condition: Bullish as long as the Iran campaign continues; an end to the Russia-Ukraine war could bring oil down.
calls.reason: Further US strikes on Iran mean more supertanker and infrastructure damage; every strike pushes oil higher.
calls.quote: Every strike pushes oil higher, and every spike lands on your wallet.

notes: Macro/geopolitical commentary; biases implied rather than stated with levels. Oil bias is implied from Iran escalation narrative.
